question: Do public museum catalogues, corpora and image archives index findable evidence for the Indus script, and which metadata fields can be joined?
outcome: Focused pass: 114 inspected inscription-confirmed original records across New Delhi 76, Kolkata 18, British Museum 6 cached witnesses, Penn 5, Louvre 4 and Met website 5; these are bounded minima. Portal seven-term union has 4007 record IDs and 158 candidate pages, yielding 94 unique originals and 10 plaster copies. Penn Indus Script filter has 34 records: 5 originals and 29 plaster impressions. 61/114 originals (53.51%) join to 61 corpus families / 67 faces; 80 carry usable identifier keys and 61/80 (76.25%) match. Audit methods: 13 exact, 6 normalized, 36 CISI published concordance, 5 shared field/plate, 1 Marshall composite. Thirty confirmed pairs selected deterministically; all 61 retained. HR 5635345 resolved via Marshall 1931 II p. 404, row 345 = HR 5635. Missing sampled metadata: bibliography 101/114, dimensions 25/114. One site, four material, five comparable dimension and nine single-face sign-count differences flagged.
challenge: British Museum and MFA requests HTTP 403; Louvre search 429 though object JSON works; NMMA timeouts; National Museum of Pakistan SSL transfer failure and no object-level inventory located. Complete institutional inscription totals remain unmeasured. Corpus identifiers include concatenated publication references and an identifier collision at DKI838; 53 sampled originals remain unjoined. Museum and corpus terminology, dimension coverage and sign segmentation differ.
remedy: Use portal internal JSON route with museumId=all, complete pagination and accession deduplication; use Met website instead of failed API; use explicit CISI museum/excavation concordances and Penn published plate references. Preserve all failed routes, source values and uncertain joins in raw storage. Record image/data rights separately; keep unresolved-rights payloads local. Keep previous pass in history/2026-10-07-depth-pass.
retry_when: Independent reviewer repeats 30 confirmed pairs and checks the full 61-row audit; functioning BM/MFA/NMMA inventories or Pakistan object-level records permit wider inscription counts; published concordances resolve the remaining 53 unjoined sampled records.
